steps.title: Construct U‑shaped harp
steps.instruction: Cut a Pt‑Ir wire to ~31 mm total length (two 9 mm arms and an 11 mm middle), flatten it between hard metal to a square cross‑section, rinse in acetone, place on a microscope slide over black‑plastic, position four nylon strings 1 mm apart across the arms, tape ends, apply thin layers of cyanoacrylate with an injection‑needle tip to fix strings, let glue harden, cut excess string at the wire edges with a scalpel, rinse in distilled water after use and remove tissue debris with tissue paper.

steps.title: Build interface storage chamber
steps.instruction: Remove nylon mesh from the sides of a 100 µm cell strainer, glue the bottom of the strainer to the bottom of a translucent plastic box with RTV118 silicone adhesive, drill a hole in the box lid, cut a 21 G injection needle to ~15 mm, insert needle through the hole and seal with RTV118, attach thin Tygon tubing to the needle distal end, verify that the mesh sits flush with the fluid level when filled, connect the needle Luer fitting to a 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ gas source with adjustable flow, sterilize the chamber after each experiment by filling with 70 % ethanol overnight, rinse thoroughly with distilled water and dry.

steps.title: Prepare recording bath chamber
steps.instruction: Glue a 50 mm diameter round cover glass to the bottom of a recording chamber using RTV118 silicone rubber sealant, apply just enough silicone to avoid pockets of air, let cure for 48 h, remove excess dried silicone, ensure the Teflon coating of the chamber is intact.

steps.title: Prepare AgCl ground electrodes
steps.instruction: Cut Ag‑wire to appropriate lengths, strip Teflon coating, handle only with clean forceps, clean any grease with acetone, connect to patch‑pipette or bath‑ground holders (solder or mechanical), immerse the distal end in 4 % NaOCl (chlorine bleach) for ≥24 h to form a light‑gray AgCl layer, handle bleach with care.

steps.title: Make intracellular stock solution IC8503 (1.25×)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.280 g CsCH₃SO₃, 0.8418 g CsCl, 0.2071 g TEA‑Cl, 0.8358 g HEPES (hemi‑Na salt), 0.0951 g EGTA in MilliQ water to 100 mL, adjust pH to 7.3 with CsOH, make up 40 mL of this 1.25× stock, aliquot 1 µL and store at –20 °C; on experiment day add 0.07134 g MgATP (for 40 mL) and 0.024654 g Na₃GTP (for 40 mL), readjust pH to 7.3, store 1 µL aliquots at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare intracellular solution IC8503 (1×) with dyes
steps.instruction: Mix 400 µL of the 1.25× IC8503 stock with 25 µL of 1 mM Alexa 594 (final 50 µM), 40 µL of 50 mM QX314 chloride (final 2 mM), add 35 µL MilliQ water to reach 500 µL total, filter through a 0.22 µm Millex syringe filter, keep on ice during experiments and store remaining aliquots at –20 °C; protect fluorescent dyes from light with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Prepare alternative intracellular stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare IC4101 (K‑gluconate based) and IC4202 (K‑gluconate + KCl) stocks as described in Recipes 5‑8, each at 1.25× concentration, aliquot 1 µL, store at –20 °C, and dilute to 1× on the day of experiment adding Alexa 488 (100 µM) or Alexa 594 (50 µM) and QX314 as needed; filter and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare reagent stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 1 M KCl (7.456 g in 100 mL water), 1 M MgCl₂·6H₂O (10.166 g in 50 mL water), 1 M CaCl₂·2H₂O (14.701 g in 100 mL water), 2 M KOH (~100 mg pellet dissolved in 1 mL water), 0.2 M KOH (0.1 mL of 2 M stock diluted to 1 mL), 100 mM CNQX (10 mg in 362 µL water), 10 mM bicuculline (50 mg in 11.96 mL water), 10 mM strychnine·1.75H₂O (201.2 mg in 50 mL water), 50 mM CPP (50 mg in 3.96 mL water), 0.3 mM TTX (1 mg in 10.44 mL water), 50 mM QX314 (10 mg in 0.67 mL water), 1 mM Alexa 594 (1 mg in 1.32 mL water), 1 mM Alexa 488 (1 mg in 1.75 mL water); store aliquots at –20 °C as indicated, protect light‑sensitive solutions, keep KOH solutions in plastic containers.

steps.title: Prepare extracellular buffer EC3000
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8.474 g NaCl, 1.247 g HEPES (hemi‑Na salt), 2.5 mL 1 M KCl stock, 2.5 mL 1 M CaCl₂ stock, 1 mL 1 M MgCl₂ stock, 1.802 g D‑glucose in MilliQ water, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 M HCl, bring volume to 1 L, store at 4 °C, use within a week (up to 10 days).

steps.title: Prepare extracellular bath EC1000
steps.instruction: In a 2 L volumetric flask add 14.610 g NaCl, 4.2 g NaHCO₃, 5 mL 1 M KCl stock, 5 mL 1 M CaCl₂ stock, 2 mL 1 M MgCl₂ stock, 3.604 g D‑glucose, fill to 2 L with MilliQ water, leave space for CaCl₂, dissolve solids, pour into a glass bottle, verify osmolality ≈300 mOsm, bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ~30 min, then add 5 mL 1 M CaCl₂ (after CO₂ saturation to avoid CaCO₃ precipitation), split into 1.8 L (no drugs) and 0.2 L (pharmacology) portions, keep both bubbled.

steps.title: Add pharmacological blockers to small EC1000 aliquot
steps.instruction: To the 0.2 L EC1000 portion add 20 µL 100 mM CNQX (final 10 µM), 200 µL 10 mM bicuculline (final 10 µM), 20 µL 10 mM strychnine (final 1 µM), 80 µL 50 mM CPP (final 20 µM); optionally add TTX to achieve 1 µM final concentration by adding 333 µL of 0.3 mM TTX stock per 100 mL bath solution. Handle all toxins with caution.

steps.title: Prepare Ames storage solution
steps.instruction: Thaw a 50 mL aliquot of Ames stock (8.8 g Ames powder in 1 L water, stored at –20 °C), pour into the storage chamber, bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ~20 min until CO₂‑saturated, add 105 mg NaHCO₃, stir until dissolved, keep chamber closed; do not add NaHCO₃ before CO₂ saturation to avoid CaCO₃ precipitation.

steps.title: Pull and fire‑polish patch pipettes
steps.instruction: Lightly fire‑polish both ends of pipette blanks with a gas flame, pull pipettes on a two‑stage puller (e.g., Narishige PP‑83) to achieve 5–11 MΩ resistance when filled with intracellular solution (heater settings NO.1 = 13.5, NO.2 = 8.3 for this puller), store in a dust‑free container, use on the same day of pulling.

steps.title: Prepare dissection area and tools
steps.instruction: Set up a 100 × 15 mm Petri dish on a dissection microscope, fill with cold EC3000 (pre‑cooled at 4 °C for ~1 h), gather scalpel holder #4, scalpel blade #20, curved scissors, small iris scissors, two watchmaker’s forceps, injection needle on a 1 mL syringe, small beaker, pasteur pipette with fire‑polished tip, and lens paper pieces (≈15 mm × 5 mm).

steps.title: Anesthetize and euthanize rat
steps.instruction: Place rat in an isoflurane anesthesia chamber, flow 100 % O₂, after ~10 min introduce isoflurane to reach 2 %–4 % concentration, confirm deep anesthesia by loss of reflexes, remove rat and perform cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Dissect eyes and isolate retina
steps.instruction: Rapidly dissect both eyes with curved scissors, rinse in a small beaker of cold EC3000, transfer eyeballs to the Petri dish under the microscope, remove extra‑ocular tissue with forceps, pierce the equatorial wall with a sharp injection needle, cut around the equator with iris scissors to separate cornea/lens (front half) from the posterior eye cup, remove vitreous from the eye cup using forceps (avoid touching retina), detach retina from choroid/sclera by inserting a blunt Pasteur‑pipette tip beneath retina and sliding sideways or by pulling peripheral sclera with two forceps, cut optic nerve with scissors, obtain a retina cup.

steps.title: Section retina into quadrants and store
steps.instruction: Using a curved scalpel, cut the retina cup through the optic disc into four equal quadrants, orient each quadrant ganglion‑cell side up, place a small piece of lens paper under each quadrant with forceps, lift the quadrant out of EC3000, lay the lens paper with retina on the nylon mesh of the storage chamber so the tissue contacts the Ames storage solution below and air above, repeat for both eyes (total 8 quadrants), close the chamber lid, verify 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ flow, let tissue rest ≥1 h at room temperature before slicing.

steps.title: Cut retinal slices
steps.instruction: Transfer one quadrant from the storage chamber to a Petri dish containing cold EC3000 (or EC1000 if bicarbonate‑buffered), ensure the retina faces down, gently remove the lens paper, trim the quadrant to a ~2 × 5 mm strip, grasp a corner with forceps and cut vertical slices (parallel to photoreceptor axis) by hand with a curved scalpel; each slice should be 100–200 µm thick, obtain 10–15 slices per quadrant, keep slices in the dish.

steps.title: Transfer slices to recording chamber
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished Pasteur pipette, gently suction one or more slices from the dish and expel them into the recording chamber, arrange slices parallel with identical orientation (photoreceptor side outward curvature), place the Pt‑Ir harp (from step 1) on top of the slices so nylon strings run orthogonal to slice long axis and each slice is crossed by 2–3 strings, secure chamber on the microscope stage.

steps.title: Start perfusion of recording chamber
steps.instruction: Place the inlet tubing’s thick Tygon end into a reservoir containing EC1000 saturated with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂, run the tubing through a micro‑filter‑candle gas bubbler, regulate flow to 1.5–3 mL/min with an adjustable clamp, position the thin Tygon outlet tubing into the chamber and start suction; ensure flow is adequate to maintain oxygenation and pH, avoid too low flow (precipitation) or too high flow (mechanical instability).

steps.title: Position ground electrode
steps.instruction: Insert the AgCl ground electrode into the bath chamber near the outlet tubing to minimize contamination of the bath solution, ensuring it does not interfere with patch‑pipette access.

steps.title: Set up microscope and locate AII cell
steps.instruction: Mount a water‑immersion objective, lower it into the bath without trapping air bubbles, turn on IR‑DGC illumination, focus on slice surface on the TV/computer monitor, move along the long axis of each slice to find a cell body in the inner nuclear layer at the INL/IPL border with a thick apical dendrite, raise the objective ~1.5 mm above the slice surface while keeping the immersion contact.

steps.title: Prepare patch pipette for recording
steps.instruction: Cut a ~1 × 30 mm strip of Parafilm, wrap it tightly around the pipette tip from the distal tip up to the shoulder, press firmly at the end, fill the tip with a few µL of the 1× intracellular solution using a melted‑tip syringe or a Microloader tip, mount the pipette in the holder, apply positive pressure (5–15 mbar) via the side port and close the valve.

steps.title: Approach cell and form GΩ seal
steps.instruction: With the objective raised, move the pipette tip into the bath, locate the tip under the microscope by moving it laterally across the field of view, lower the tip just above the slice surface, then bring it into focus, gently touch the cell body (observe a small depression), release positive pressure, apply gentle suction (mouth or syringe) and/or hyperpolarize the pipette to obtain a ≥2 GΩ seal, monitor resistance, neutralize pipette capacitance with the C‑fast circuitry, set holding potential to –60 or –65 mV.

steps.title: Break into whole‑cell configuration
steps.instruction: Apply a brief (≈0.1 ms) high‑amplitude (≈400 mV) suction pulse (press ZAP button) to rupture the membrane, confirm whole‑cell by appearance of large capacitive transients and increased steady‑state current, neutralize cell capacitance with C‑slow circuitry, estimate series resistance and fine‑tune if needed, keep bath fluid level low to reduce pipette capacitance.

steps.title: Verify AII electrophysiological signature
steps.instruction: From a holding potential of –60 or –65 mV, apply a brief 5–10 mV depolarizing pulse; the presence of an unclamped action current confirms an AII amacrine cell; protect fluorescent dyes from light until after recording; optionally maintain a slight negative pressure (≈–0.7 mbar) to reduce endocytosis.

steps.title: Set liquid junction potential
steps.instruction: Enter the calculated liquid junction potential of +7.3 mV (bath relative to pipette) into the Patchmaster software before starting the test pulse.

steps.title: Configure test pulse and baseline
steps.instruction: In Patchmaster, set a test pulse of 5 mV amplitude, 5 ms duration, click SETUP, adjust voltage offset to zero baseline current, record pipette resistance for documentation.

steps.title: Design capacitance measurement stimulus (baseline)
steps.instruction: Create a PGF sequence with five segments: (1) sine wave at Vhold = –90 mV, 2 kHz, ±20 mV, 2000 ms; (2) constant Vhold, 20 ms; (3) depolarizing step to –10 or –20 mV (e.g., 100 ms) to open Ca²⁺ channels; (4) constant Vhold, 100 ms to allow conductance recovery; (5) sine wave at Vhold = –90 mV, 2 kHz, ±20 mV, 10 000 ms. Use sampling interval 50 µs (20 kHz), set low‑pass filter cutoff to 2 × f_sine (4 kHz), set number of points per cycle to 10, skip the first cycle, average 1 cycle, total cycles ≈24 440. Set V‑reversal to –15 mV.

steps.title: Configure lock‑in amplifier settings
steps.instruction: In Patchmaster LockIn window set Mode = Sine + DC, Calibration = Manual, Phase Shift = 0°, Attenuation = 1.000, enable generation of traces for CM, GM, GS, DC, set default Y‑ranges (Real Y = 200 n, Real Z = 1.000, Imag Y = 200 n, Imag Z = 1.000, Admit Y = 200 nS, Imp Z = 1.000 Ω), Phase = 180°, V‑rev = –15 mV.

steps.title: Acquire data and perform leak subtraction
steps.instruction: Run the PGF sequence, acquire membrane capacitance (C_m), membrane conductance (G_m) and series conductance (G_s) per sine‑wave cycle; optionally add a leak‑subtraction protocol (three‑segment stimulus: constant Vhold, scaled depolarization ≤ –60 mV, constant Vhold) and subtract scaled leak current in analysis (e.g., IGOR Pro) as described.

steps.title: Optional: arbitrary waveform stimulation (Q)
steps.instruction: Generate an arbitrary voltage waveform (e.g., EPSP) as a template file, configure two DA channels in Patchmaster: Channel‑1 for sine‑wave lock‑in stimulus, Channel‑2 for the arbitrary waveform (output to EXTERNAL STIM INPUT VC), sum the two outputs, set Vhold = –90 mV, sine wave parameters as in step 23, arbitrary waveform inserted between constant segments, ensure timing matches; connect DA‑6 to the amplifier’s external stimulus input.

steps.title: Optional: dual‑cell synaptic experiment (R)
steps.instruction: Use a quad‑amplifier (e.g., EPC10‑USB‑Quadro), mount one pipette with IC4202 for a rod bipolar cell (set liquid junction = +14.5 mV) and another with IC4101 for an AII amacrine (junction = +14.5 mV), locate a connected pair, establish GΩ seals and whole‑cell configurations for both, test connectivity with a two‑sweep PGF (chemical/electrical), then run baseline sine‑wave (dCmABbaseline) and EPSP‑evoked capacitance (dCmABepsp) sequences as described, using rapid mode‑switching commands (VC → CC → VC) and appropriate lock‑in settings.

steps.title: Calibrate phase shift and attenuation of EPC10
steps.instruction: Warm up the EPC10 ≥60 min, perform standard amplifier calibration, attach MC 10 model cell (ON‑cell mode), generate a calibration sine‑wave PGF matching experimental frequency, set LockIn to Manual, write results to Notebook, note measured phase shift, subtract 90° to obtain instrument phase shift, keep attenuation = 1.0; compensate C‑fast to 0.01 pF, run calibration again (first measurement ≈0 pF), de‑compensate C‑fast by a known amount (e.g., 2 pF), run calibration again, adjust attenuation until measured capacitance change equals the de‑compensation amount, optionally repeat for several de‑compensation values and fit a line to obtain attenuation; for multiple frequencies, send phase‑shift and attenuation values from Patchmaster Protocol Editor using commands L LockInPS xxx and L LockInAtt yyy.

steps.title: Finalize and clean up
steps.instruction: After recordings, gently rinse the harp and chamber with distilled water, remove tissue debris with tissue paper, store reusable components (harp, pipettes, electrodes) appropriately, discard used solutions according to safety regulations, clean all glassware, and document all parameters and observations in the lab notebook.
